result.summary:
Full S1-S14 pass over REQ-019 (profile capture as a resumable step-by-step form, consent gate, optional-field rule), at branch feature/WF02-REQ-019, commit 2e212ca. Read docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md and security-invariants.md in full first. Read docs/agents/design/REQ-019.md and REQ-019-schema.md, then git diff master...HEAD myself (28 files, apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts, apps/bot/drizzle/0004_fancy_zombie.sql, apps/bot/src/domain/{profile,onboarding}.ts+tests, apps/bot/src/handlers/{profile,start}.ts+tests, i18n additions, index.ts) rather than trusting REVIEWER's Step 2b report (handoffs/WF02-REQ-019/step-02b-reviewer-regate.json), though I did read it for context on what it already covered.

S1 (PRIMARY FOCUS) -- PASS. Re-derived the derive-then-gate discipline directly in apps/bot/src/handlers/profile.ts's three callback handlers (makeProfileSkipCallbackHandler, makeProfileStudentCallbackHandler, makeProfileExperienceCallbackHandler) and the two generic listeners (makeProfileTextAnswerHandler, makeProfileContactHandler): every one of them re-fetches flowUser fresh from tgId, computes hasConsented/hasChapter/profile fresh, calls determineOnboardingStep (domain/onboarding.ts) fresh, and gates the write on step.kind==='profile-field' && step.field===<claimed field> BEFORE calling any write function -- confirmed by reading the actual code (profile.ts lines ~532-617), not the design's prose claim about it. domain/onboarding.ts's advanceOnboarding never reads profiles at all while !hasConsented (ternary short-circuit to null), so a consent-less caller structurally cannot reach a write path regardless of what callback_data claims.

Own adversarial scenarios beyond REVIEWER's Step 2b coverage (REVIEWER already live-verified: forged profile:skip:phone + forged free-text answer, both with consent_pd_at IS NULL, against real Postgres -- I did not repeat those, I re-verified new ones). Built a throwaway vitest file (apps/bot/src/handlers/__security_adversarial.test.ts, NOT committed -- deleted immediately after use, confirmed by `git status --porcelain` returning empty) that dispatches real bot.handleUpdate() calls through the actual compiled handlers against a real scratch Postgres (docker compose up -d, port 55432, drizzle-kit migrate applied cleanly -- 0004_fancy_zombie.sql included). Four scenarios, all passed:

1. Field-mismatch (not just consent-missing): a fully-onboarded-through-required-fields user whose real next step is 'phone' receives a forged `profile:skip:email` callback. Result: neither emailSkipped nor phoneSkipped changes -- the gate's step.field==='email' check fails against the actual derived step ('phone'), so no write function is ever called. This is the concrete case REVIEWER's own coverage did not test (REVIEWER tested consent-missing, not step-mismatch under valid consent).
2. Replay of an already-honored skip: profile:skip:phone is answered once (phoneSkipped becomes true, step advances to 'email'), then the identical stale profile:skip:phone callback_data is replayed. Result: phoneSkipped stays true (no duplicate write), and critically emailSkipped stays false -- the replay is NOT reinterpreted as answering the new current field ('email'); the gate compares the callback's claimed field ('phone') against the current derived field ('email'), they mismatch, so it is a pure no-op followed by a harmless re-prompt for email.
3. Chapter-but-no-consent via /profile directly (bypassing /start): seeded a User with chapterId set via assignChapter() but consent_pd_at left NULL (an inconsistent/adversarial DB state), then dispatched a bare /profile command. Result: determineOnboardingStep checks !hasConsented before ever looking at hasChapter (domain/onboarding.ts line ~42-44), so the single reply sent is the consent prompt, not any profile-field prompt, and getProfileByUserId(user.id) returns null -- zero profiles rows written. Confirms consent is checked unconditionally first regardless of what chapter state exists, closing exactly the scenario named in my task brief.
4. Own re-verification (not a repeat, a fresh construction) of the forged-skip-while-unconsented case using a freshly created (never-consented) user via resolveOrCreateUser + a direct forged profile:skip:phone callback with no /start ever run: zero profiles rows written.

S0.2's reading of 'declining consent' (re-showing the same Agree-only prompt, no dedicated Decline button) is a stated, flagged design assumption (REQ-019.md §8.2), not a security defect -- consistent with the invariant's own text ('no write before consent'), which is what matters for S1.

S2 -- N/A, reason: no role/EventStaff authorization surface is touched by this diff; /profile-family commands operate only on the calling user's own row (see S3).

S3 -- PASS. Traced every read in handlers/profile.ts: getProfileByUserId(db, flowUser.id) is called ONLY with flowUser.id, and flowUser is resolved ONLY via getFlowUserByTgId(db, BigInt(ctx.from.id)) -- the caller's own Telegram identity, never a value taken from callback_data, command arguments, or any other user's id. profile:chapter:<id> callback data carries a chapterId (public, not secret), never a target user id. formatProfileDump is only ever invoked on this same self-resolved profile. No list/search/export surface is added by this diff. Confirmed no cross-user read path exists.

S4 -- N/A, no token/InviteCode generation or validation in this diff.

S5/S6/S7 -- N/A, no check-in/admission/capacity code touched.

S8 -- N/A, vacuously, confirmed structurally: grepped writeAuditLog across every changed file (handlers/profile.ts, domain/profile.ts, domain/onboarding.ts, handlers/start.ts) -- zero matches. Matches design §0.3's explicit claim (profile field writes are not an authorization-relevant status transition); I verified this by grep rather than trusting the design doc's assertion.

S9/S10 -- N/A, no notification/broadcast code touched.

S11 (PII never logged) -- PASS. Grepped the full diff for console.*/log.* calls: apps/bot/src/index.ts has console.error((err as Error).message) (pre-existing config-load failure path, carries only an Error.message string, never touches profile/PII data, unchanged surface) and log.info('bot starting') (pre-existing, no fields). Zero log/console calls exist anywhere in handlers/profile.ts, domain/profile.ts, or domain/onboarding.ts -- the design's S11 commitment (REQ-019.md §6, 'no function interpolates phone/email into a log message') holds trivially because no logging call exists in this code at all, confirmed by grep, not by reading the design's promise. AC5's concrete negative case (invalid email format) was independently exercised in my adversarial run's setup path and confirmed the rejected value is used only for isValidEmailFormat and never written, echoed, or logged (matches domain/profile.ts lines ~142-147 and handlers/profile.ts's email branch at ~459-470, which sends only the fixed catalog.profile.invalidEmailFormat string). log.ts's REDACTED_KEYS ('phone','email') mechanism (apps/bot/src/log.ts) is unchanged and correct as defense-in-depth, though this diff's own code never reaches it since it never calls the logger with profile data at all. formatProfileDump's plain-text phone/email echo is a direct reply to the same user about their own data (S3's exception, correctly cited in REQ-019.md §2.5) -- confirmed formatProfileDump is called only in the self-resolved /profile and /profile_edit paths (handlers/profile.ts lines ~227, ~296), never from any handler operating on another user's id.

S12 -- N/A, no CSV export code touched.

S13 (migration sign-off, explicit) -- SIGNED OFF, PASS. Read apps/bot/drizzle/0004_fancy_zombie.sql directly (not a description of it): 11 statements total -- 6 `ALTER TABLE profiles ALTER COLUMN <col> DROP NOT NULL` (first_name, last_name, company, position, is_student, experience_level) and 5 `ALTER TABLE profiles ADD COLUMN <col>_skipped boolean DEFAULT false NOT NULL` (phone/email/links_github/links_linkedin/links_site). No DROP COLUMN, no RENAME, no data-rewriting statement, no other table touched -- matches REQ-019-schema.md §5's exact predicted statement list and §4's column-change summary verbatim. This is a pure widen-nullability + additive-boolean-column migration: it deletes no personal-data content, rewrites no existing row's stored value (DROP NOT NULL touches only the constraint, not the data; ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT backfills a non-PII boolean), and does not retroactively change any past event's published attendance/show-rate figures (profiles carries no attendance data; that lives in registrations, untouched here). S13's actual target (drop/rewrite of PII or attendance history) does not apply to this migration -- confirmed by reading the raw SQL myself, not accepting DATA-DESIGNER's or BACKEND-DEV's characterization of it.

S14 -- N/A, publish_consent column and publication surface untouched by this diff.

Zero-active-chapters fix (REVIEWER rework, commit 244c9e1) -- re-traced for a consent-ordering regression: in all three modified call sites in handlers/start.ts (makeStartHandler, makeChapterCallbackHandler, makeConsentCallbackHandler), the `hasChapter = true` override (when assignChapterOrPrompt returns 'continue', including the zero-active-chapters branch) is only ever reached INSIDE an `if (!hasChapter)` block that itself only executes after that call site's own pre-existing consent gate already passed (makeStartHandler's chapter branch runs only for an already-consented returning user; makeConsentCallbackHandler's chapter branch runs only after recordConsent was just called in the same handler invocation, above this code). No path reaches the chapter-assignment/hasChapter-override logic while consent is still unset -- the fix widens what 'chapter satisfied' means for that single pass, it does not change when chapter logic runs relative to consent. No regression found.

Build verification (run myself, real output, fresh scratch Postgres): `docker compose up -d` (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml) + bounded pg_isready poll (ready in <5s) + `DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx drizzle-kit migrate` (11 migrations applied cleanly). `npm run lint` (apps/bot) -- 0 errors. `npm run build` (apps/bot) -- tsc clean. `npx vitest run` (full suite, TEST_DATABASE_URL set) -- 288/288 passed when run with `--no-file-parallelism`; without that flag, 1 of 288 failed (start.test.ts's first zero-active-chapters case, an off-by-one in captured-message count) due to a cross-test-file race against the SAME shared scratch Postgres (multiple *.test.ts files TRUNCATE the same tables concurrently under Vitest's default per-file worker parallelism) -- reproduced twice, then confirmed by re-running with --no-file-parallelism (all pass). This is a test-infrastructure/harness gap (shared mutable DB across parallel test workers), not a defect in this diff's security properties -- it is orthogonal to and compounds the already-filed docs/issues/ISS-0013.yaml (CI has no Postgres service at all). Flagging as a new finding for ORCH to file as its own issue (recommend: either force sequential/no-file-parallelism for DB-backed suites, or give each DB-backed test file its own schema/connection) -- not filed by me directly per core-directives.md's id-allocation rule.

No issue in this diff itself blocks S1-S14. All applicable items PASS or are correctly marked N/A with a stated reason; S13 sign-off explicitly given.

issues.title: DB-backed vitest suites race when run with Vitest's default per-file parallelism against the shared scratch Postgres
issues.description: apps/bot/src/handlers/start.test.ts (and any future DB-backed *.test.ts file) TRUNCATEs profiles/users/chapters in its own beforeEach against the single shared docker-compose Postgres instance. Under Vitest's default per-file worker parallelism, another test file's concurrent TRUNCATE/INSERT can interleave with this file's assertions, producing a flaky, non-deterministic failure (reproduced: 1/288 tests failed without --no-file-parallelism, 0/288 with it, across two runs). Not a defect in WF02-REQ-019's own code or security properties -- purely a shared-mutable-test-DB race. Recommend either running DB-backed suites with --no-file-parallelism (or vitest.config's fileParallelism:false) in CI/local scripts, or giving each DB-backed test file an isolated schema/connection. Compounds, but is distinct from, the already-filed docs/issues/ISS-0013.yaml (no Postgres service in CI at all).
